claims.statement: Tests must never depend on external services: Redis, outbound HTTP APIs, SMTP and DNS are mocked or stubbed across the backend, and all API calls are mocked on the frontend; the ephemeral testcontainers PostgreSQL instance (or TEST_DATABASE_URL) is the only allowed infrastructure dependency, so a test that performs a real network, Redis or SMTP call is broken by definition rather than something to fix by requiring the service.

pytest configuration in pyproject.toml keeps output low-volume (-q, --tb=line, --no-header, --no-summary, --disable-warnings, --show-capture=no) while always collecting coverage of src with a JSON report at coverage.json and the terminal report suppressed; coverage uses branch tracking and omits tests/* and migrations/*.

tests/ is organized by domain and by architectural layer, with routers/, services/, repositories/, tasks/, market/ (including market/commands/), account/ (including account/commands/ and account/csv/), auth/commands/, commands/ for the top-level CLI commands (seed_data, flush_market_data), integration/brokers/, email/, ws/, shared fixtures/, and root-level files covering app startup, settings, logging, request IDs and migration drift.
tests/conftest.py sets SECRET_KEY, ENVIRONMENT=test and STUB_EXTERNAL_API=true in os.environ before importing anything from src, so settings validation and the app factory see a test configuration.

Database fixtures give a session-scoped PostgreSQL service (reusing TEST_DATABASE_URL when it is a Postgres URL, otherwise starting a PostgresContainer for postgres:17-alpine and rewriting the driver to postgresql+asyncpg), a function-scoped test_engine that rebinds sessionmanager's engine and sessionmaker to the test database and creates the full schema per test before dropping it afterwards, a function-scoped db_session that rolls back, and seed_reference_data that commits AccountTypeModel and InstitutionModel reference rows.

The autouse session-scoped global_mocks fixture forces Huey into immediate mode so tasks run synchronously without a broker, patches ConnectionManager.init_redis/close/send_personal_message/send_personal_message_sync on the class (stashing the originals as _orig_* attributes), and patches src.main.init_worker_dashboard and src.main.close_worker_dashboard to avoid real AsyncRedis connections whose aclose() costs roughly four seconds per test.

The autouse function-scoped fake_redis_manager fixture replaces the Redis client on the shared src.core.redis.redis_manager singleton plus the src.auth.api and src.auth.service default_redis_manager singletons with an in-memory FakeRedis/FakeRedisManager, and mock_redis_storage exposes that backing store for assertions, so no test needs a Redis server or DNS; tests exercising the real RedisManager construct their own instance.

tests/fixtures/auth.py supplies MockEodhdGateway (a MarketGateway implementation returning fixed price/search payloads via StubEodhdGateway), an authenticated auth_client carrying a UserApi-issued bearer token and an unauthenticated client, both built on ASGITransport + LifespanManager against the real app with the eodhd gateway factory and EmailService.send_verification_email patched, plus test_user and other_user fixtures for ownership/authorization tests.

tests/test_migrations_autogenerate.py cleans the database, runs alembic upgrade head, runs alembic revision --autogenerate, and asserts the generated migration contains no op.* calls to prove models and migrations are in sync, deleting the generated file in a finally block.

The Vitest setup in frontend/vite.config.ts runs jsdom with environmentOptions.url http://localhost/, loads src/setupTest.ts, includes src/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,ts}, minimizes output with the dot reporter and silent 'passed-only', and collects v8 coverage as JSON over src/**/*.{js,ts} with skipFull.

frontend/src/setupTest.ts imports @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest, spies on console.warn to drop only messages containing bits-ui's derived_inert warning while forwarding every other argument to the captured original, waits 50 ms in an afterAll hook so bits-ui's pending body-scroll-lock timer fires before the jsdom environment is destroyed, and stubs window.location with a URL('http://localhost/')-derived object exposing href/origin/protocol/host/hostname/port/pathname/search/hash plus assign/replace/reload/toString spies.

Frontend tests are colocated with the code under test and mock framework and third-party modules unavailable under jsdom — SvelteKit runtime modules such as $app/paths, $app/navigation, $app/forms and $app/stores, and lightweight-charts (with Path2D/ResizeObserver polyfills and stubbed createChart time scale, price scale, series and primitive attach).

scripts/agent-test implements a three-gate model: Gate 0 pre-flight lint/type checks that halt the harness without running tests on failure, Gate 1 targeted fail-fast single-path runs with backend coverage disabled, and Gate 2 full regression (auto-detecting ecosystems from the git diff, or --all) that parses JUnit XML / Vitest JSON reports and renders an Index of counts and failed identifiers plus Traces for the first 1-2 failures under a default 3000-character cap.
The agent harness covers only the backend and frontend ecosystems — the Go indicator service is verified by its own CI job running go vet, go build and go test in services/indicator-service.

CI runs three independent jobs: backend (Python 3.14, uv sync --dev, ty check, ruff check + ruff format --check, pytest) with no Redis and no database service because Redis is faked and PostgreSQL is supplied by testcontainers; frontend (Node 25, npm install, npm run check, npm run lint, npm run test:run with VITE_* and JWT_SECRET env); and indicator-service (Go 1.27 vet/build/test).

All development commands must run inside Docker via docker compose exec <backend|frontend>, and before committing the area guides require lint, type checks, formatting and tests; a model edit additionally requires an Alembic autogenerate migration, with the agent harness the preferred entrypoint and the raw pytest/vitest commands the fallback.

Email tests patch src.core.email.aiosmtplib.SMTP at the transport boundary (and patch the settings object for SMTP configuration) while the template suite renders verify_email templates through src.core.email.jinja_env with no transport at all, and broker integration tests drive src/stubs/wealthsimple.py stubs (StubWealthsimpleAPI, StubWSAPISession) instead of making network calls, keeping SMTP and broker HTTP traffic out of the suite.

frontend/src/setupTest.ts installs a no-op Element.prototype.scrollIntoView stub because jsdom does not implement it while bits-ui's Command calls it asynchronously on the active item and on the closest group heading; without the stub those calls reject with 'closestGroupHeader?.scrollIntoView is not a function' and vitest reports them as unhandled errors for any test rendering a grouped Command.

Service-layer frontend suites follow the mandated mocking pattern by mocking the API module itself (vi.mock('@/api/marketService', () => ({ getMarketService: vi.fn() }))) and then handing back a hand-built client whose every method is a vi.fn() — search, createOrUpdateSecurity, getWatchlists, createWatchlist, renameWatchlist, updateWatchlistSort, deleteWatchlist, addSecurityToWatchlist, removeSecurityFromWatchlist, reorderWatchlistSecurities, addToWatchlist, removeFromWatchlist — which lets a plain class such as WatchlistService be exercised without SvelteKit runtime modules or network access; HoldingsService uses the same shape against $lib/api/accountService.

Gate 0 of scripts/agent-test runs exactly 'uv run ruff check --output-format concise', 'uv run ruff format --check' and 'uv run ty check --output-format concise' for the backend and 'npx svelte-kit sync', 'npx svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json --output machine', 'npx eslint . -f json' and 'npx prettier --check .' for the frontend, halting with sanitized diagnostics and exit code 1 before any test runs; both test gates parse reports written to .cache/agent-test (backend.xml JUnit XML, frontend.json Vitest JSON) and the process exits 1 when any test failed, errored, or the runner itself failed.

Backend tests reach the Go indicator sidecar only through stubbed transports rather than HTTP: tests/market/test_indicator_client.py drives IndicatorServiceClient through an httpx.MockTransport handler (and patches httpx.AsyncClient.post for the single-owned-client case), while tests/market/test_indicator_compute_api.py patches IndicatorServiceClient.compute with an AsyncMock to assert candle aggregation and interval handling on the compute endpoint.

Which mocking seam a frontend suite uses follows how the code under test obtains its client: fetch-based API clients mock global.fetch and assert URL/method/payload plus error mapping (apiClient, accountClient, authService, indicatorsService, snapshotsService); service classes that pull a client from a module factory mock that module and return a hand-built client (watchlistService, holdingsService); and service classes that receive their collaborators as constructor arguments need no module mock at all — ChartDrawingsService.test.ts constructs the service with stubbed patchPreferences, createSnapshot/getSnapshots, a toast double and vi.fn() callbacks, then asserts tool mutual exclusion, Delete/Backspace/Escape handling, undo/redo, drag coalescing and legacy-anchor normalization without a write-back.

Route-level frontend suites come in page.server.test.ts / page.svelte.test.ts pairs: the server suite mocks the API service modules and drives load/actions with a hand-built Cookies and RequestEvent object (asserting that /holdings never loads holdings in the server load and falls back to HOLDINGS_TABLE_DEFAULT_CONFIG on preference failure), while the component suite renders the page with render(Page, { props: { data } }) and asserts the shell-first contract — skeleton rows before the post-navigation load resolves, rows filling in without user action, sequential page loading, per-currency totals — and the 401 path that calls goto('/auth/login?clear_session=true'); src/lib/api/async-data.test.ts unit-tests that redirect seam directly.

Frontend suites also mock third-party and browser-facing modules (mode-watcher, @simplewebauthn/browser, qrcode, $env/static/private) and use vi.hoisted when a mock must exist before the imports are evaluated; src/hooks.server.test.ts is the one suite that opts out of jsdom with a '// @vitest-environment node' pragma to verify JWT handling with jose, Path2D and ResizeObserver polyfills are declared locally at the top of the chart suites, and window.matchMedia is defined inside src/routes/layout.test.ts.

Chart plugin suites import only types from lightweight-charts and hand-build IChartApi/ISeriesApi doubles plus a canvas target that records draw calls, then exercise the four layers frontend/AGENTS.md requires: state transitions and delegate firing, mouse-adapter hit-testing and drag lifecycle, renderer geometry and canvas draw calls under a bitmap coordinate scope, and the full primitive lifecycle (attached/detached/destroy, updateAllViews, hitTest cursor resolution, TimeProjector projection of future whitespace).

Where the application resolves collaborators through its svcs registry rather than a module-level factory, backend suites override the registry directly: tests/market/test_search_router.py registers AsyncMock/MagicMock replacements for SecuritySearchCache and MarketGateway on app.state.svcs_registry to assert cache-hit and cache-miss behaviour of the market search endpoints without an outbound call.

Cache suites that receive a Redis client by constructor inject their own local fake instead of relying on the singleton fake_redis_manager: tests/market/test_indicator_cache.py defines its own FakeRedis and casts it to IndicatorCache, and tests/market/test_security_search_cache.py passes an AsyncMock into SecuritySearchCache.

Backend async suites are marked with either @pytest.mark.anyio or @pytest.mark.asyncio, and both anyio and pytest-asyncio are dev dependencies, so neither marker is globally enforced by configuration (pyproject.toml sets no asyncio_mode or anyio_backend fixture).

tests/fixtures/account.py seeds the shared relational fixtures (accounts, portfolios, positions, securities and integration users) and includes cross-user variants — other_user_account, other_user_portfolio and other_user_external_user, all bound to the other_user fixture — so ownership and authorization denials can be asserted, while tests/fixtures/market.py seeds watchlists for the test user.

Frontend test imports use two interchangeable path aliases — SvelteKit's $lib/* and the shadcn-style @/* — where @/* maps to ./src/lib/* through the kit.alias entry in frontend/svelte.config.js, so vi.mock specifiers may be written either way for the same module.
